title: Rental supply reaches seven-year high despite sector exits
summary:
Britain's private rental sector has lost almost 850,000 properties over the past decade, with 181,000 sold in 2025 alone. Despite this, rental supply has reached a seven-year high in 2026, driven primarily by build-to-rent developments rather than traditional landlord stock.

title: Tenancy deposit scheme TDS appoints new chief executive
summary:
The Dispute Service has announced a change in leadership as chief executive Steve Harriott retires after 16 years. Jacqueline Starr will succeed him at the end of 2026, taking over as the private rented sector adjusts to recent regulatory changes.

title: Protest disrupts National Landlord Investment Show
summary:
Tenant advocacy groups disrupted the 100th National Landlord Investment Show in London, demanding rent controls. The incident highlighted ongoing divisions between landlords and housing campaigners over rental market policy.

title: Winkworth reports uneven trading amid uncertainty
summary:
Estate agency franchise Winkworth has reported uneven trading in recent months, citing political and economic uncertainty as factors weighing on market confidence. The company expects revenues and pre-tax profits to remain in line with market expectations for the year.

title: Chelsea development completes after decade of planning
summary:
Magnet Capital has completed a £1,009,475 development finance loan for a two-bedroom property behind King's Road in Chelsea. The project required 21 Party Wall Awards and took over a decade to secure planning permission within a conservation area.

title: GB Bank completes £33m London bridging facility in seven days
summary:
GB Bank has completed a £33 million bridging finance facility secured against a mixed-use London property portfolio, delivering the funding within seven days to meet an exchange deadline. The borrower, an established property investor with more than £500 million worth of real estate holdings, required the funding to support a wider acquisition strategy.

title: Estate agent ordered to pay £790 over undisclosed buyer
summary:
The Property Ombudsman has ordered an estate agent to compensate buyers £790 after failing to disclose the existence of a competing purchaser during a property transaction. The case highlights transparency obligations under industry codes of practice.

title: Digital signatures uptake stalls in conveyancing sector
summary:
The implementation of Qualified Electronic Signatures for property transactions has faced significant challenges, with only five registrable dispositions completed in the first quarter of 2026. Industry experts have warned that current Land Registry guidance contains fundamental flaws hampering adoption across the conveyancing sector.

title: Landlords face first Making Tax Digital deadline
summary:
Landlords and sole traders face the first Making Tax Digital quarterly deadline on 7th August, with accountants warning that confusion remains over the new requirements. The scheme became mandatory from April 2026 for those with qualifying income above £50,000.

The post Landlords face first Making Tax Digital deadline appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Scottish landlords face year-long tribunal delays
summary:
Landlords in Scotland are experiencing waits of up to 12 months to regain possession of their properties through the housing tribunal system, according to legal practitioners. Law firm Aberdein Considine reports that landlords are typically waiting between eight and 12 months from submitting an eviction application to receiving a tribunal hearing, with legal costs reaching approximately £10,000 before cases conclude.
